clue.text: Actors entertained by more expansive media person

indicators.note: to be entertained by is to be taken in as a guest, so the actors go inside the other word

parts.note: broader means wider or more expansive
a cast is the body of actors in a production

explanation.surface: A theatre company is hosted by a larger, more expansive media personality.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who presents programmes on radio or television is a media figure.

clue.text: Julius Caesar, perhaps — male getting off horse

indicators.note: the male letter gets off, leaving the rest of the word behind

parts.note: Julius Caesar is an example of a Roman

explanation.surface: Julius Caesar dismounts from his steed.
explanation.definitionFit: A roan is a horse whose coat has white hairs mixed through a darker colour.

clue.text: Declare man to be turned off

parts.note: to aver is to declare or assert
Ted is a man's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: A man is announced as having been switched off.
explanation.definitionFit: Averted eyes are ones turned away, the past participle matching 'turned off'.

clue.text: Shy, keeping outside society, or comfortable?

indicators.note: the word for shy keeps the society letter while staying outside it

parts.note: coy means shy or bashful

explanation.surface: Is a timid person who avoids society actually just comfortable?
explanation.definitionFit: Cosy describes a snug, homely sense of comfort.

clue.text: Dolly is dancing in a sensible manner

indicators.note: the letters move about as dancers do, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A girl named Dolly dances in a calm, sensible way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges DOLLYIS, the letters of 'Dolly is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Solidly here means soundly or dependably, the way a sensible person acts.

clue.text: Get cut up with minimal marks in test

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to axe something is to cut it

indicators.note: the minimal part of the word marks is its first letter alone

explanation.surface: A student gets upset at scoring almost nothing in a test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns AXE into EXA; 'minimal' keeps just the M of 'marks'. 'Get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam is a formal test of knowledge.

clue.text: Board must take measures, we hear, when there's forgery

parts.note: a counter is a board or surface in a shop or kitchen

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for taking measures is said aloud, not written

parts.note: a tailor takes measures to fit a suit, so fit can mean take measurements

explanation.surface: A company board must act when fraud is uncovered.
explanation.walkthrough: The last syllable of the answer, FEIT, is pronounced like FIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A counterfeit is a fake copy passed off as genuine, a forged item.

clue.text: Alas a dream's going wrong for African city

indicators.note: a plan going wrong falls apart, so the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Sadly, a traveller's dream of Africa goes awry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going wrong' rearranges ALASADREAMS, all the letters of 'Alas a dream's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dar es Salaam is the largest city of Tanzania in East Africa.

clue.text: Being put off, I speak pompously and get worse

parts.note: to deter is to discourage or put someone off
to orate is to speak in a grand, pompous manner

explanation.surface: Discouraged, a speaker talks grandly and things go downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: To deteriorate is to decline in quality or condition.

clue.text: Awful bigots named in surprise news headline

indicators.note: awful suggests the letters are in a terrible mess and must be put right

explanation.surface: Dreadful bigots are named and shamed in a shock headline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' rearranges BIGOTSNAMED, the letters of 'bigots named'.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalists cite this phrase as the classic example of an unusual story, since the reverse is not news.

clue.text: Dim reply nut concocted in a foolish way

indicators.note: something concocted is mixed up from its ingredients, so these letters are remixed

explanation.surface: A dim-witted nutcase cooks up a silly reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concocted' rearranges DIMREPLYNUT, the letters of 'Dim reply nut'.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting imprudently means acting rashly, without sensible caution.

clue.text: Sign appeal put to soldiers

parts.note: O is an exclamation of appeal or entreaty, as in 'O Lord'
men is a common word for soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: A recruiting poster appeals to soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a sign or portent of what is to come.

clue.text: Saw ten coming out hurt

indicators.note: the ten letter comes out of the word, leaving a gap that closes up

parts.note: a saw is an old saying, a maxim
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A woodworker watches ten fingers come out of the saw injured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' is not the tool or the verb but a proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: To maim is to injure or wound badly.

clue.text: Girl meeting queen, originally born less well off

parts.note: nee, used before a woman's maiden name, means born with that name originally
Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen

explanation.surface: A girl born into poverty is introduced to the queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Needier means poorer, having greater want of money.

clue.text: Bird lacking courage when head is chopped off

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which is removed here

parts.note: craven means cowardly, lacking courage

explanation.surface: A cowardly bird loses its head to the chopper.
explanation.definitionFit: A raven is a large black bird of the crow family.

clue.text: Give rough treatment to clothing

definitions.meaning: to hit hard or treat roughly
British slang for clothes or gear

explanation.surface: A rough handling is given to someone's outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense means to batter someone, the slang noun sense means one's clothes or kit.

clue.text: Cold girl showing high social standing

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: An aloof young woman displays her upper-crust status.
explanation.definitionFit: Class can mean elegance or high rank in society, as in 'a touch of class'.

clue.text: Hang about with daughter and friend

parts.note: an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: Someone loiters with their daughter and a companion.
explanation.definitionFit: To dally is to dawdle or waste time lingering.

clue.text: One picture obscures another

indicators.note: one film obscuring another means it hides a word within its letters

explanation.surface: One film overshadows a rival release.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obscures' points to letters concealed across 'One picture'. The definition 'another' means another picture.
explanation.definitionFit: An epic is a grand, large-scale film, so it is another kind of movie.

clue.text: Boss is good person with university degree

parts.note: ST, for saint, is the crossword good person
D can stand for degree, as in a doctorate

explanation.surface: The manager is a decent sort who holds a degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' is not the manager but a raised knob or stud, as on a shield.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is an ornamental knob, the same thing as a decorative stud.

clue.text: Time to relax with one having a bit of fun

definitions.text: one having a bit of fun

parts.note: to ease is to relax or loosen

explanation.surface: Time off to unwind with a friend who is a bit of a joker.
explanation.definitionFit: A tease is someone who playfully mocks or provokes others for amusement.

clue.text: Upsetting bulletin about old soldier

indicators.note: about means round, so the old letter goes inside
in a down clue, upsetting means turning the word upside down so it reads upwards

parts.note: a bulletin is a news report

explanation.surface: Disturbing news about an elderly veteran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upsetting' turns REPORT into TROPER; 'about' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A trooper is a cavalry soldier or private in an armoured unit.

clue.text: Moral learner? I cheat terribly to begin with

indicators.note: to begin with places the mixed-up letters at the start, ahead of the learner
terribly implies the letters are badly mangled and need reordering

parts.note: L, as on a learner driver's plate, stands for learner

explanation.surface: A supposedly upright student admits cheating badly at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moral' is the definition; the question mark only marks the surface's sly hint at a dishonest student. 'to begin with' puts the shuffled letters ahead of the learner.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethical means principled, in line with right conduct.

clue.text: Feeling hopeless on behalf of miss Doone almost

parts.note: for can mean on behalf of, as in acting for someone

indicators.note: almost means the name stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: Lorna Doone is the heroine of R. D. Blackmore's Exmoor romance

explanation.surface: Someone pines in despair for a lost girl named Doone.
explanation.walkthrough: Lorna Doone is the title heroine of an 1869 English novel set on Exmoor.
explanation.definitionFit: Forlorn describes someone sad and without hope, abandoned.

clue.text: Instruction not to change boy's hat

parts.note: stet, Latin for 'let it stand', tells a printer to leave the text unchanged
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: Someone orders that a lad's headgear must not be altered.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stetson is a wide-brimmed cowboy hat.

clue.text: Enthusiastic about Britain, totally? Only partially

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is used, so the letters sit within the two words

explanation.surface: Is someone wholly keen on Britain, or just half-hearted?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Only partially' points to letters running across 'Britain, totally'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be into something is informal for being keen on it.

clue.text: Curse issued by goatherd

indicators.note: the letters are issued from inside the word, coming out of it

explanation.surface: A goatherd lets fly with a swear word.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath can be a swear word, a profane exclamation.

clue.text: Positive response you offered with interjection

parts.note: ye is an old form of you
ah is an interjection expressing realisation or pleasure

explanation.surface: You give a cheerful reply with an exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeah is informal for yes, an affirmative answer.

clue.text: Former German politician's eye make-up

definitions.meaning: Helmut ... was chancellor of West Germany and then reunited Germany, from 1982 to 1998
a black powder used to darken the eyelids and lashes

explanation.definitionFit: Helmut Kohl was the German chancellor who oversaw reunification; kohl is also dark cosmetic powder for lining the eyes.

clue.text: Keen to have surgery — keyhole for this?

indicators.note: having surgery rearranges the inside of something, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient eager for an operation wonders if minimally invasive surgery suits this joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to have surgery' rearranges the letters of 'Keen'. Keyhole surgery is commonly done on this joint, so the definition is a cryptic hint.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthroscopic or keyhole surgery is very often performed on the leg joint below the thigh.

clue.text: Activity for cosmetic purposes to get on escreaming

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Activity for cosmetic purposes to get on escreaming' is garbled ('escreaming' is no word); the double definition looks like 'Activity for cosmetic purposes' plus 'screaming', but the words between cannot be accounted for and no source gives the printed clue
annotationWithheld.clue: Activity for cosmetic purposes to get on escreaming

clue.text: Ploughman who has an interest in company performance?

definitions.text: Ploughman who has an interest in company performance?

parts.words: Ploughman who has an interest in company performance?
parts.note: a ploughman grips the blade of his plough; read differently, the phrase describes an investor who owns part of a business

explanation.surface: A farmer keeps a close eye on how his firm's shares are doing.
explanation.walkthrough: A ploughshare is the cutting blade of a plough, so a ploughman literally holds a share.
explanation.definitionFit: An investor owning stock in a firm benefits from its results, while the ploughman grips the ploughshare.
